project.name: Savage Wind Multiplayer
project.distribution: Savage Wind fork builds with native multiplayer compiled in
project.upstream_update_policy: project owner manually integrates new Savage Wind releases

architecture.transport_candidate: libdatachannel v0.24.6 for native M1 source builds
architecture.invite_flow: clipboard invite and reply, public STUN address discovery, direct ICE
architecture.integration: isolated multiplayer core with small build, settings, UI, runtime, and guest-site adapters

milestones.name: Native multiplayer build and internet lobby
milestones.scope: Owner accepted M1 after Windows and Linux clients joined a friend hosting on Linux. Hosting from the owner's network still requires diagnosis.
milestones.open_verification: owner-host direction, selected ICE candidates and full native acceptance matrix

milestones.name: Remote Link presence
milestones.scope: Plateau position, facing and native idle, walk and jump are verified in Windows direct sessions. Read-only health snapshots and the F1 roster display are implemented. Equipment and the full acceptance matrix are pending.

implemented: explicit packet header codec and validation
player snapshot codec
eight-peer session state
per-peer per-channel sequence filtering
connection-scoped transport interface
control payload codecs with bounded UTF-8
compatibility handshake, host roster, and lobby lifecycle
deterministic mock transport with bounded queues and state faults
synthetic multiplayer tests
in-process eight-Link demo
bounded libdatachannel transport with separate ICE and lobby deadlines
verified HTTPS rendezvous client and expiring invite service
copied admitted roster with local lobby and remote slot generations
strict 1.9.0 guest hook for asynchronous Great Plateau placeholder creation and indexed deletion
native Windows/Linux source build with localized F1 and System > Options multiplayer controls
one persisted default-off setting and window-thread teardown when multiplayer is disabled
per-peer Great Plateau NPC placeholders for the native M1 build
direct single-use clipboard invite and reply with public STUN discovery
M2 position and facing snapshots at up to 20 Hz with host batching and roster epoch validation
Plateau remote Link proxy using a local RomFS actor alias and the native matrix setter
native idle, walk and jump playback on each owned Plateau proxy
current quarter-heart observation and display in the F1 multiplayer roster
not_implemented: remote Link appearance pieces, extended action mapping and broader area support

Leave, same-slot rejoin, host reboot cleanup, and independent inventory opening passed. The 60 FPS target run verified area withdrawal and return.
last_verified.m2_plateau_animation: Two Windows Vulkan instances with gamelib 34aa482dae306a0d played native idle, walk and jump both ways over direct WebRTC. One renderer sustained all seven fixture-driven proxies for 30 seconds after START. The 60/90/120 targets were exercised below sustained 90/120 FPS.
